summary: A small computer model, rather than tests on people, gave Tegaserod medium risk scores of 50 for the liver and 51 for the heart [M]. Tegaserod was pulled from the market starting in 2007 in the United States and two other countries due to heart harm and neurotoxicity, which is damage to the nervous system [3]. In addition, clinical studies were stopped early because of rules suspending the drug's use in 2007, as well as low patient sign-ups in 2005 [5][6][7].
